THEME INTRODUCTION
Engineering Scale. 
Powering Possibilities. 
Amber’s journey reflects a continuous pursuit of deeper integration, stronger technological capability, 
and greater ownership across the value chain. What began as a manufacturing enterprise has evolved 
into a diversified engineering platform, spanning across consumer durables, electronics, and railway 
subsystems & defence applications.
This evolution is built on a strategy of expanding engineering capabilities, strengthening backward 
integration, and building component-level expertise. This pursuit strengthens the Company’s ability 
to participate more meaningfully in its customers’ value creation, and to be a trusted manufacturing 
partner.
Scale and efficiency remain central to this journey, as the Company expands capacity and 
manufacturing capabilities, to drive operating excellence across its operations.
The essence of Engineering Scale, Powering Possibilities: A commitment to building capabilities 
that translate into consistent execution and sustainable growth.

MANAGEMENT MESSAGE
Executive 
Chairman  
& CEO’s 
Statement
Jasbir Singh
Executive Chairman,  
CEO and Whole Time Director
Amber Enterprises India Limited
Dear  
Stakeholders,
I am proud to present our Annual Report 
for the Financial Year 2025-26. The 
year underscores the resilience of the 
Amber Group, supported by the strength 
of our diversified business model 
and the disciplined execution of our 
strategic priorities. Despite a challenging 
environment, all three business Divisions 
delivered growth, reinforcing strength 
in our diversification strategy and in our 
long-term growth prospects. 
Building on our strength in the Room Air 
Conditioning industry, we have further 
diversified our growth drivers through 
strategic acquisitions, partnerships, 
and expansion initiatives. This year 
marks an important milestone in Amber 
Enterprises’ evolution, reinforcing our 
standing as a diversified manufacturing 
group with a growing EMS footprint.
The strategic stake acquisitions and 
partnerships with Power-One, Shogini 
Technoarts and Unitronics, Israel, coupled 
with the expansion plan of Ascent Circuits 
and the Ascent-K Circuit facilities under 
our Electronic Division, have laid a strong 
foundation for Amber’s evolution journey.
We are steadily advancing into a future-
ready enterprise, offering comprehensive 
B2B manufacturing solutions across 
Consumer Durables, Electronics, Railway 
Subsystems and Defence.
In June 2026, the Company entered into a 
Manufacturing Collaboration Agreement with OPPO 
Mobiles India Private Limited, under which it will 
undertake manufacturing of mobile phones for the 
OPPO, OnePlus, and Realme brands, strengthening 
Amber Group’s position as a comprehensive 
manufacturing solutions provider.  
This initiative will further strengthen our portfolio 
while maintaining the right balance between high 
percentage margin-low volume and low percentage 
margin-high volume with high ROCE businesses.

Economic Environment
The macroeconomic environment 
during Financial Year 2025-26 remained 
complex, shaped by geopolitical 
uncertainties, supply chain disruptions, 
and volatility in commodity markets. 
Despite these challenges, India’s 
structural fundamentals continued to 
demonstrate resilience, supported by 
robust domestic demand, sustained 
infrastructure investments, and a 
conducive policy framework.
Complementing these strong economic 
fundamentals, policy initiatives such as 
the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) and 
Electronics Component Manufacturing 
Scheme (ECMS) are playing a pivotal 
role in advancing the Government’s 
‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’ vision. By fostering 
domestic manufacturing capabilities 
and promoting deeper component-
level integration, these initiatives are 
enhancing India’s competitiveness 
and positioning the country as a global 
manufacturing hub.
For Amber, the Government’s progressive 
policy framework has been a key catalyst 
of our expansion plan. It has enabled us 
to deepen our presence in the electronics 
component ecosystem, undertake 
strategic capacity expansion, and 
strengthen our participation in advanced 
manufacturing segments. Supported 
by focused capital investments and 
capability enhancement initiatives, 
we are well positioned to capitalise 
on continued strengthening of India’s 
electronics manufacturing ecosystem.Consumer Durables
The Government’s GST rationalisation 
initiative, resulting in a reduction in GST 
on Room Air Conditioners from 28% to 
18%, is expected to enhance affordability, 
expand consumer access and accelerate 
penetration. Additionally, the RAC 
industry transitioned during the year to 
the revised BEE rating norms effective 
January 2026, marking a key shift 
toward enhanced energy efficiency and 
sustainable cooling solutions.
During the year, we augmented the Room 
AC manufacturing capacity at Sri City in 
Andhra Pradesh. In the Commercial Air 
Conditioning business, we continued 
to strengthen our Light Commercial AC 
portfolio through product innovation 
including the expansion of our inverter 
ductable range, the introduction of One-
Way Cassette ACs, and the addition of 
new customers.
While the RAC industry got impacted by 
non-conducive weather conditions during 
the year, our Consumer Durables Division 
demonstrated remarkable operational 
resilience driven by a diversified product 
offering, wallet share gain and continued 
expansion of product portfolio.Electronics
Our Electronics Division continued to play 
a pivotal role in Amber’s growth journey 
into a technology-led comprehensive 
B2B manufacturing enterprise. During 
the year, we strengthened our position 
across the electronics value chain through 
strategic investments and partnerships 
with Power-One, Unitronics, and Shogini 
Technoarts, expanding both horizontally 
into new growth avenues and vertically 
into deeper capabilities. 
Power-One
The strategic investment in Power-One 
Micro Systems expands our addressable 
market in the growing Power Electronics 
segment, encompassing Solar Inverters 
(On-grid, Off-grid, and Hybrid), UPS 
Systems, EV Chargers (AC & DC), and 
Battery Energy Storage Systems. This 
partnership deepens our presence across 
the renewable energy and industrial 
power ecosystem, while leveraging our 
EMS expertise to drive greater backward 
integration within the segment.
Unitronics
The strategic investment in Unitronics, 
based in Israel, broadens our Electronics 
Division’s portfolio into growing Industrial 
Automation applications. This expands 
our presence across HMI, PLC, PLCs with 
integrated HMIs, and SaaS solutions, 
while expanding our global footprint and 
deepening our presence in high-value, 
technology-led segment.
Shogini
The strategic investment in Shogini 
Technoarts, based out of Pune, 
Maharashtra, further strengthens our 
presence in the multi-layer Bare PCB Divisional Overview

Financial Year 2025-26 marked another 
year of strong progress for the Company, 
with consolidated revenue crossing 
the `12,000 Crore milestone despite a 
challenging operating environment for 
the RAC industry. The performance of 
all three business divisions highlights 
the effectiveness of our diversification 
strategy and reinforces the resilience of 
our divisional mix. 
Consolidated revenue grew by 22% 
year-on-year, increasing from `9,973 
Crore in Financial Year 2024-25 
to `12,186 Crore in Financial Year  
2025-26. Operating EBITDA grew by 
22%, from ` 796 Crore in the previous 
year to `970 Crore in Financial Year 
2025-26, driven by improved operating 
performance and a favourable shift 
towards higher-margin products.
The Reported Profit After Tax (PAT) for 
the year stood at ` 226 Crore, in Financial 
Year 2025-26 as against the ` 251 Crore 
in Financial Year 2024-25. The Reported 
PAT was impacted by the exceptional 
one-off impairment of investment 
(including loan) in Shivaliks Mercantile; 
and the share of loss JV of Shivaliks 
Mercantile. Before the impact of these 
items, the underlying performance of the 
business remained strong reflecting the 
resilience and strength of our diversified 
portfolio.
During the year, we strengthened our 
balance sheet through two significant 
capital raises. Amber Enterprises raised 
equity capital of ~` 1,000 Crore from In Financial Year 2025-26,

Performance over the Years
Amber continued to strengthen its 
market position by expanding its product 
portfolio, enhancing its manufacturing 
capabilities, and investing in innovation 
and R&D. Building on this foundation, the 
Company strengthened the RAC segment 
through a diversified portfolio spanning 
across Split ACs, Inverter ACs, and fast-
growing commercial cooling solutions 
such as Ductable Tower and Cassette Air 
Conditioners. Beyond completely built air-conditioning systems, the Company 
caters to a wide range of components, 
reinforcing its position as a comprehensive 
and integrated solutions provider. 
Despite a weather-impacted and 
challenging RAC industry during the year, 
the Division outperformed the industry, 
delivering a resilient 14% revenue growth. 
This was driven by deepening wallet 
share with existing customers, migrating 
gas-charging clients to full Original Design Manufacturer (ODM) solutions, 
and expanding the Light Commercial 
AC product portfolio. To capitalise on 
increasing demand and the long-term 
growth prospects of the RAC industry, 
the Division expanded its Room Air 
Conditioner (RAC) manufacturing capacity 
at its new Sri City facility, strengthening 
its ability to support future growth.

Performance over the Years
The Electronics Division delivered a 
strong performance in Financial Year 
2025–26, with revenue growing by 49% 
and Operating EBITDA by 89%, driven 
by strong business growth and addition 
of the new businesses acquired during 
the year. The Company accelerated its 
growth strategy through a combination 
of horizontal and vertical integration 
initiatives, strengthening its position 
across the electronics value chain. 
The acquisitions of Power-One Micro Systems, Unitronics (Israel), and Shogini 
Technoarts expanded the Division’s 
presence into complementary growing 
segments.
Power-One Micro Systems has 
strengthened the Division’s capabilities 
in Power Electronics and Energy 
solutions, while Unitronics has expanded 
its global Industrial Automation footprint 
through Human-Machine Interfaces 
(HMIs), Programmable Logic Controllers 
(PLCs), and Automation solutions. Shogini Technoarts has enhanced the 
Division’s manufacturing capabilities and 
capacity expansion in multi-layer Printed 
Circuit Boards (PCBs), further deepening 
its participation in the electronics 
manufacturing ecosystem. 
The year marked a significant step in 
the Division’s strategic evolution, with 
key initiatives enhancing its presence 
in high-value industrial and electronics

ABOUT THE ESG REPORT
Building Trust through   
Transparent Reporting
Amber is pleased to present its Environmental, Social and Governance Report for the Financial Year ending 31st March 2026. This report 
has been prepared to provide our stakeholders with a transparent, comprehensive and meaningful account of Amber's sustainability 
commitments, ESG performance and the progress made during the reporting period across our operations and value chain.
Throughout this report, Amber and its subsidiaries* are collectively referred to as ‘Amber’ or ‘The Company’ unless stated otherwise, 
the disclosures encompass Environmental, Social, Governance and operational performance across Amber's manufacturing locations 
and business operations within the defined reporting boundaries.
We Value Your Feedback
Amber is committed to open and transparent engagement with all its stakeholders. 
We welcome feedback, questions and comments regarding the disclosures and 
performance presented in this report. Stakeholders are invited to reach out to us 
through the following:
Email: info@ambergroupindia.com or cs_corp@ambergroupindia.com
Reporting Period
The sustainability performance disclosed in this report covers the period from  
1st April 2025 to 31st March 2026, consistent with Amber's annual reporting cycle for 
monitoring, evaluating and transparently disclosing ESG progress to our stakeholders.
Reporting Frameworks and Alignment
This report has been prepared with reference to the Global Reporting Initiative 
Standards and is aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals 
and India's National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct. These recognised 
frameworks provide a consistent and comparable structure for ESG disclosure,  
enabling stakeholders to assess Amber's sustainability performance with confidence, 
clarity and context.
*For the boundary on the subsidiaries included in the ESG Report please refer to Page No. 186 of the BRSR.

ESG STRATEGY AND MATERIALITY ASSESSMENT
Driving Sustainable Growth
through Strategic Priorities
Amber’s ESG strategy is built on a clear conviction that long-term business success and positive 
environmental and social impact are mutually reinforcing. Sustainability is embedded in the way 
the Company operates, invests and grows, ensuring that business decisions create lasting value for 
stakeholders while strengthening organisational resilience.
The Company’s ESG strategy is anchored in three strategic pillars: Sustainable Environment, 
Empowering People and Society and Responsible Governance. Together, these pillars provide a 
structured framework to define priorities, establish targets, allocate resources, monitor performance 
and drive continuous improvement across operations and the value chain.
Prioritising ESG Issues 
that Matter Most
To ensure its sustainability efforts 
remain focused and impactful, Amber 
undertakes a structured materiality 
assessment to identify and prioritise 
the ESG topics that are most significant 
to its business and stakeholders. The 
assessment enables the Company 
to focus on issues with the greatest 
potential to influence long-term value 
creation, risk management and business 
resilience.
The outcomes of the materiality 
assessment directly inform Amber's 
ESG strategy, guiding decision-making, 
target setting, resource allocation and 
performance monitoring. Recognising 
the evolving nature of sustainability 
risks and opportunities, the Company 
periodically reviews its material topics 
to reflect changes in the regulatory 
landscape, market dynamics and 
stakeholder expectations, ensuring 
its ESG priorities remain relevant and 
future-ready.Grounding Strategy in 
Materiality
The priorities that shape Amber's ESG 
strategy are grounded in a structured 
materiality assessment that identifies 
the ESG topics most significant to the 
Company and its stakeholders. By 
evaluating both business relevance 
and stakeholder expectations, the 
assessment ensures that sustainability 
priorities remain strategically focused, 
responsive to an evolving business 
environment and aligned with long-term 
value creation.
Recognising that material issues evolve 
with changing regulations, market 
dynamics and stakeholder expectations, 
Amber periodically reviews and updates 
its material topics. This ongoing process 
enables the Company to strengthen 
its ESG strategy, address emerging 
risks and opportunities and ensure its 
sustainability agenda remains relevant 
and future-ready.Materiality Assessment 
Process
Amber follows a structured three step 
approach to identify, assess and prioritise 
material ESG topics:
Systematic Mapping
The first stage involved systematic 
mapping of ESG topics through industry 
benchmarking, peer analysis, and 
alignment with leading national and 
international sustainability frameworks
Stakeholder Engagement
The second stage involved targeted 
stakeholder engagement to capture 
external perspectives on the significance 
of identified topics. 
Internal Prioritisation
The third stage involved internal 
prioritisation, where management 
evaluated each topic against business 
relevance, risk exposure, and strategic 
importance to arrive at a validated set of 
material issues.

Amber’s waste management strategy is

Material Optimisation and Circularity
Material optimisation is embedded within Amber’s manufacturing practices to 
maximise resource efficiency and minimise waste generation. The Company 
continuously improves production processes to optimise material utilisation 
while reducing dependence on virgin and hazardous materials wherever 
feasible. The Company also promotes the reuse of materials such as plastic 
boxes, cartons and oils, extending material life and supporting circular economy 
principles. Process-level improvements further reduce material losses, 
optimise input consumption and minimise packaging waste across operations.
Key Circularity Initiatives across Manufacturing Sites
Amber continues to translate its circular economy commitments into practical 
initiatives across its manufacturing facilities.
DDN-6, Dehradun: Waste plastic is reused for evaporator spare packaging, 
reducing packaging costs, improving durability during transport and lowering 
environmental impact.
Sricity: Scrap foam sheets from PCB packaging are repurposed as heat 
exchanger coil separators, resulting in the reuse of 1.56 kg of material every 
month through an in-house initiative.
Jhajjar-2: The elimination of polybags from packaging has saved 2.42 Lakh 
polybags and approximately `6.8 Lakh annually, while reducing packing time 
by 10 seconds per kit and supporting compliance with Extended Producer 
Responsibility (EPR) requirements. Together, these initiatives demonstrate 
Amber's commitment to embedding circular economy principles into day- to- day 
manufacturing operations through practical, measurable improvements.

Assessment (HIRA): Identification 
and evaluation of workplace risks 
across operations to prioritise 
critical safety concerns

defined timelines, accountability 
and closure tracking

committees responsible for

monthly meetings •  Audits and Inspections: Regular

and Gemba Walks conducted by 
EHS and site teams to identify gaps 
and ensure compliance 
EHS teams and site management 
jointly oversee the implementation 
of corrective and preventive actions,

risks and continuous monitoring of 
workplace safety performance. Amber

and Security Single Points of Contact 
(SPOCs) across manufacturing locations.

coordinated emergency response and 
consistent implementation of safety 
protocols throughout the organisation.

regular internal audits further reinforce 
statutory compliance and continuous 
improvement across all facilities.

expectations, enabling consistent and transparent governance across the organisation and its subsidiaries.

Amber continues to strengthen its sustainability governance framework, ensuring ESG considerations are integrated across 
strategy and operations. A multi-tier governance model integrates Board level oversight with execution at business and site-levels. 
The governance model includes Board and senior leadership oversight of ESG priorities, business and plant level accountability 
for implementation and ESG cluster SPOCs who drive site-level initiatives. During the Financial Year, Amber further enhanced this 
framework by strengthening cross-functional coordination and increasing employee participation in sustainability initiatives.
The Board, through the Business Responsibility and Sustainability (BR&S) Committee, oversees ESG strategy, sustainability risks and 
disclosure requirements, while dedicated sustainability teams and ESG SPOCs coordinate implementation across business units. This 
governance structure enables timely identification of ESG risks and opportunities while strengthening accountability across operations.

Manufacturing Industry Overview
The Indian manufacturing industry represented a defining phase in the Financial Year 2025-26, underpinned by the government’s 
sustained focus and policy initiatives aimed at strengthening domestic component manufacturing and backward integration. This 
evolution reflects the maturation of the ‘Make in India’ initiative, as the emphasis progressively shifts beyond assembly towards 
building component-led capabilities domestically.
Amid a complex geopolitical environment shaped by supply chain realignments, volatile commodity cycles, and evolving trade 
dynamics, the Indian economy demonstrated resilience, supported by increasing localisation, import substitution, and the development 
of domestic manufacturing capabilities across key sectors.
This structural shift was supported by strong domestic demand and the government’s continued thrust on capital expenditure across 
key sectors, alongside the Production Linked Incentive (PLI), Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) and various 
other central and state government incentive schemes. Together, these measures augur well for a sustained cycle of investment, 
employment generation, and enhanced domestic value addition.
Room Air Conditioner 
(RAC) Market
The Indian Room Air Conditioner 
(RAC) continues to be one of the  
under-penetrated product categories 
among the Consumer Durable segment, 
increasingly transitioning from an 
aspirational purchase to a household 
necessity. While the industry is 
inherently seasonal and influenced by 
weather conditions, its low penetration 
combined with underlying macro 
drivers such as rapid urbanisation and 
rising temperatures, continue to gain 
momentum. During the year, demand 
remained subdued amid non-conducive 
weather conditions; however, the 
structural fundamentals of the market 
remain firmly intact.
The long-term outlook for the Indian RAC 
industry remains compelling, supported 
by favorable structural drivers such as  
rising incomes, increasing urbanisation, 
low penetration levels and the growing 
preference for energy-efficient cooling 
solutions.

Low Household Penetration1
RAC penetration in India remains significantly lower than in several comparable Asian markets. At around 12%, this relatively low 
penetration highlights the substantial headroom for growth in the Indian RAC market. Favourable demographic fundamentals 
and evolving consumption patterns are likely to support the growth, creating a significant multi-decade opportunity for the 
industry. India’s middle class is expanding, and middle-class and affluent consumers are expected to account for 93% of total 
consumer spending by 2036. Rising affluence, urbanisation and the increasing prevalence of nuclear families is expected to 
accelerate residential housing demand, which, in turn, is likely to drive demand for Room Air Conditioners (RACs).
(Sources: https:/ /www.fortuneindia.com/business-news/expect-india-to-remain-top-residential-air-conditioning-market-global-
ly-for-lg-electronics-co-official/143172 https:/ /www.weforum.org/stories/business/massive-urban-shift-in-india-consumer-growth-de-
centralizing/)
GST Rationalisation Boosting Affordability2
The Government of India undertook a significant GST rationalisation initiative, resulting in a reduction in GST rates across 
several categories, including RACs, where the rate was reduced from 28% to 18%, effective September 2025. The rate cut 
has enhanced affordability, supporting first-time adoption among price-sensitive consumers. It has also improved access to 
premium, energy-efficient 5-star models, for the expanding middle class, thereby strengthening the industry’s long-term 
growth prospects.
Rising Temperatures3
Over the years, evolving climatic conditions characterised by rising ambient temperatures, extended summer 
seasons, and increasing occurrence of heatwaves across the Indian subcontinent have fundamentally shifted 
consumer perception. Cooling is no longer viewed as a discretionary luxury but a basic necessity for health,  
well-being, and indoor productivity. Long-term climatic trends, with prolonged summers, are driving households to place 
greater emphasis on air conditioning for enhanced comfort, thereby accelerating both first-time adoption rates and the 
replacement cycle for older and less efficient units.Key Growth Drivers

Real Estate Expansion and Urbanisation4
The sustained expansion in residential real estate, including the expansion of housing societies in Tier II and III cities, 
combined with rapid urbanisation is creating a strong structural demand for RAC installations. India’s urban population 
has grown from ~31% in 2011 to ~36% in 2025 and is projected to exceed 40% by 2030. Rising lifestyle aspirations and a 
demand for better indoor thermal comfort are effectively transitioning Room Air Conditioners from a discretionary luxury to 
a fundamental household necessity, supporting more sustained and broad-based demand for cooling solutions.
Per Capita GDP Trajectory5
The economic purchasing power of the average Indian consumer is rising swiftly, with Per Capita GDP climbing from ~US$ 
2,591 in 2024 to a projected ~US$ 2,812 by 2026 and further projected to hit US$ 4,047 by 2030. As disposable income 
crosses a critical economic threshold, it enables accessibility to a broader segment of consumers, supporting both first-time 
purchases and multi-room air-conditioning within the households.

Outlook
Looking ahead, the Indian Room Air Conditioner (RAC) market is positioned for sustained, structural expansion over the medium 
to long-term. With current household penetration at approximately 12%, the industry holds a visible runway, driven by cooling 
increasingly being viewed as a necessity rather than a luxury. Alongside the rise of the middle class and improving affordability, 
continued urbanisation, residential real estate development and shifting temperature patterns, these factors are expected to 
further drive the adoption of cooling solutions in the coming years, while also contributing to a longer seasonal window for the 
RAC market.
PLI Scheme Momentum6
The Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for white goods has provided a significant impetus to accelerating investments, 
deepening supply chains, and strengthening India’s position as a manufacturing destination. With an expected cumulative 
investment of ` 11,198 Crore across the value chain, domestic value addition is targeted to rise from 20-25% to 75-80%.
(Source: http:/ /pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2217743&reg=3&lang=1)
Evolving Trends in Energy Efficiency7
Rising electricity consumption for cooling and increasing sustainability awareness are accelerating the shift towards energy-
efficient air conditioners. This transition has been further supported by the implementation of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency’s 
(BEE) revised Star Labelling standards in January 2026, which mandate higher energy performance benchmarks. As consumers 
increasingly prioritise energy savings and efficient cooling, demand for energy-efficient RACs continues to strengthen.

Key Growth Drivers
Rising Adoption of Electronics Content1
Increasing electronics content across products and applications, along with the growing adoption of smart and connected 
devices, is emerging as a key driver of demand for the domestic electronics industry. Driven by rising disposable incomes, 
rapid urbanisation, digitalisation, and evolving consumer preferences, the demand for electronic products continues to 
expand across sectors. Additionally, the government’s sustained focus on import substitution, domestic value addition, and 
local manufacturing is strengthening India’s electronics ecosystem, creating long-term growth opportunities for EMS and 
ESDM players.
ECMS: Component Ecosystem Build-Out2
The increased ` 40,000 Crore outlay for the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS), announced in the 
Union Budget 2026-27, marks a decisive push towards localisation. Focused on critical components such as PCBs, passive 
components, electro-mechanical components, sub-assemblies, camera modules, optical transceivers, and capital goods 
required for electronics manufacturing, the scheme is expected to attract investment commitments exceeding ` 1.15 lakh crore 
and generate production worth over ` 10 lakh crore. It is also expected to create more than 1.4 lakh direct jobs while advancing 
India’s vision of a self-reliant and globally competitive electronics manufacturing ecosystem.
Expansion of Automotive Electronics and the EV Ecosystem3
The accelerating shift towards connected mobility and adoption of Electric Vehicles (EVs) are driving a structural increase in 
electronic content per vehicle, including telematics, connectivity features, security features, infotainment, and powertrain 
electrification. Rigorous quality compliance and industry qualification protocols create a high threshold for participation, 
fostering a quality-driven and technologically advanced manufacturing ecosystem.
Digitalisation and Digital Infrastructure4
Accelerating digitalisation and the expansion of digital infrastructure are emerging growth opportunities for the electronics 
industry. The increasing adoption of cloud computing, connected technologies, digital services and data centres is driving 
demand for a broad range of electronic hardware, networking equipment, power management solutions, and supporting 
infrastructure. These trends are expected to create opportunities across the electronics manufacturing value chain, supporting 
its long-term growth.

are creating a more competitive, resilient and self-reliant rail ecosystem while enabling faster infrastructure development and 
greater private sector participation.

Business Overview
Amber Enterprises India Limited (‘Amber’ , 
‘the Company’ or ‘Amber Group’ including 
its subsidiaries and joint ventures) has 
evolved into a diversified, backward 
integrated and technology-led B2B 
manufacturing solutions provider, with 
capabilities spanning across three 
business segments: Consumer Durables, 
Electronics, and Railway Subsystems and 
Defence.
Over the years, the Company has 
transitioned from a Room Air Conditioner 
(RAC)-focused manufacturer to a 
diversified B2B multi-industry solutions 
provider, underpinned by deeper 
value-chain integration, expanding 
technological capabilities, and calibrated 
vertical and horizontal expansion into 
high-growth segments. 
The Company’s operating structure is 
anchored across three core business 
Divisions:
Consumer Durables: The Consumer 
Durables Division is a highly backward 
integrated B2B solution provider in 
the air conditioner segment, offering Complete Built Units (CBUs) across Room 
and Commercial Air Conditioners along 
with a wide range of RAC and Non-RAC 
components. Backed by strong R&D 
capabilities and extensive backward 
integration, the Division commands 
deep manufacturing capabilities and 
cost competitiveness, positioning it as 
a trusted manufacturing partner to the 
leading MNC and domestic brands.
Electronics: The Electronics Division is 
evolving into a comprehensive electronics 
solutions provider, with capabilities 
spanning across EMS (PCB-Assembly & 
Box Build), Bare PCBs, Power Electronics 
solutions and Industrial Automation 
solutions, serving a broad and diversified 
customer base including consumer 
durables and consumer electronics, 
automotive, telecommunication, 
aerospace and defence, energy and power, 
and industrial applications. The Division 
is further strengthening its capabilities 
through capacity expansion in multi-layer 
bare PCBs and advancing towards the precision manufacturing of complex High 
Density Interconnect (HDI) PCBs.
Railway Subsystems and Defence: 
The Railway Subsystems and Defence 
Division, operating through Sidwal, is a 
leading solution provider of advanced 
HVAC solutions for Railways, Metros 
and RRTS. Beyond the cooling solutions, 
the Division has significantly expanded

Operational Performance and Revenue Mix
The progress of the Company’s diversification strategy is reflected in its evolving revenue mix. While the Consumer Durables segment 
continues to provide a strong and growing baseline, the strategic shift towards electronics and mobility-led segments is progressively 
reshaping the composition of the business.
Railway Subsystems and Defence
During the year, the Railway Subsystems and Defence 
Division recorded a revenue growth^ of 19%, reaching  
` 535 Crore, up from ` 450 Crore in Financial Year  
2024-25. Operating EBITDA* for the year stood at 
` 90 Crore, reflecting a growth of 8% over the previous 
year. The Division continued to witness encouraging 
momentum across the Railway, Metro, and Defence 
segments, supported by an expanding product portfolio 
and healthy order book visibility.
Electronics
During the year, the Division recorded strong revenue 
growth^ of 49%, reaching ` 3,268 Crore, compared to 
` 2,194 Crore in Financial Year 2024-25. Operating 
EBITDA* registered a strong growth of 89%, reaching  
` 287 Crore. This performance was supported by strong 
PCBA and Bare PCB businesses coupled with the 
incremental contribution from Power-One Micro Systems, 
Unitronics and Shogini Technoarts.
Consumer Durables
The Consumer Durables segment maintained its strong 
growth momentum despite the underlying Room Air 
Conditioner (RAC) industry remaining largely flattish during 
the year owing to weather conditions. The Company 
demonstrated resilience and outperformed the broader 
industry. During the year, the Division recorded a revenue 
growth^ of 14%, reaching ` 8,383 Crore, compared to  
` 7,329 Crore in Financial Year 2024-25. Operating EBITDA* 
for the year stood at ` 593 Crore, reflecting a growth of 
6% over the previous year, supported by deepening wallet 
share and an expanding product portfolio.

supply higher-value, digitally integrated components.IoT and Smart Appliance 
Transition
The Indian government’s PLI scheme has played 
a transformative role in strengthening domestic 
manufacturing. The scheme is expected to significantly 
increase RAC domestic value addition to 75-80% from 
20-25%, while robustly fostering backward integration. 
This momentum is being further accelerated by the 
Electronic Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS). 
Approvals under ECMS are providing a localisation boost 
by incentivising the production of critical components. 
Together, these policies are enabling comprehensive 
component ecosystem, reducing import dependence, and 
fortifying the broader domestic supply chain.Air conditioners are steadily transitioning from a luxury 
in India to a necessity. Driven by structural factors 
including low household penetration, Rising temperature, 
urbanisation, growing middle class, and power adequacy, 
among others, the RAC industry is expected to witness 
long-term growth. Additionally, the replacement cycle 
for ACs, with consumers upgrading more frequently to 
energy-efficient models, is further supporting demand.Boost from Government’s 
Progressive Policy FrameworkSurging Demand for Room Air

creates a significant multi-year growth opportunity for

Internal Control Systems and their Adequacy
The Company has established a comprehensive internal control framework, commensurate with the scale, complexity, and 
regulatory requirements of its operations, designed to safeguard assets, ensure the integrity of financial reporting, and 
support compliance with applicable laws and regulations. The Company’s ERP system forms the backbone of its digital control 
environment, enabling standardised processes, real-time data visibility, and system-enforced approval workflows across its 
manufacturing facilities.
The Audit Committee oversees the internal control environment and has mandated independent internal audits across all 
manufacturing facilities, conducted by external auditors on a periodic basis, covering the design and operating effectiveness 
of key financial, operational, and compliance controls. Observations arising from these audits, together with management’s 
corrective action plans, are reported to the Audit Committee, which monitors implementation and reviews the overall adequacy 
of the risk management and financial reporting systems on an ongoing basis.
Based on the assessments carried out during the year, the Board is of the opinion that the Company has maintained an adequate 
and effective system of internal financial controls, which was operating effectively as of 31st March 2026.
Human Resources
The Company’s growth is anchored in the strength, adaptability, and capabilities of its people. As it expands across diverse 
and technology-intensive segments, the Company continues to build a workforce that is aligned with its evolving business 
complexity and growth ambitions. The Company’s people strategy is centred on capability building, leadership development, 
and future-readiness. Structured learning interventions, cross-functional exposure, and targeted leadership programmes are 
designed to deepen technical expertise while preparing talent for scaled operations. This is complemented by a strong focus 
on continuous learning and performance orientation, enabling employees to contribute effectively in a dynamic manufacturing 
environment.
The Company is committed to fostering an inclusive and collaborative workplace, where diversity of thought and experience 
drives innovation and decision-making. The Company has also initiated AI-focused training programmes to enhance digital 
competencies across the organisation, equipping employees with the skills to leverage emerging technologies, improve 
productivity, and drive innovation in an increasingly technology-driven business environment.
Employee engagement remains a key priority, supported by well-defined career pathways, performance-linked rewards, and 
opportunities for skill enhancement. The Company also places strong emphasis on workplace safety, ethical practices, and 
employee well-being, ensuring a secure and supportive environment across its operations.
As the Company continues to expand, its focus remains on building a resilient, agile, and future-ready workforce, capable of 
supporting its transition into a diversified, technology-led manufacturing platform.

INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
The Indian air conditioning industry navigated a challenging 
Financial Year 2025–26, as the demand got adversely 
impacted owing to weather conditions, however, the structural 
fundamentals of the market remain firmly intact.
While the industry is inherently seasonal and influenced by 
weather conditions, the structural drivers including rising 
temperatures, urbanisation, growing middle-class aspirations, 
and India’s still-low household AC penetration  remain firmly in place and continue to underpin the industry’s long term growth 
potential.
Against this backdrop, your Company delivered a resilient 
performance, with consolidated revenues growing 22.19%   
year-on-year in the Financial Year 2025–26. For a detailed 
review of the Company’s multi-segment performance, 
including business-wise developments and key operational 
achievements, please refer to the MD&A and Narrative sections 
of this Annual Report.

DIVIDEND AND DIVIDEND DISTRIBUTION POLICY
The Board of Directors has not recommended any final 
dividend, nor declared any interim dividend during the Financial 
Year 2025–26. This decision has been made after careful 
consideration of the Company’s strategic priorities and long-
term growth objectives. 
During the Financial Year 2025 -26, the Company undertook 
significant capital expenditure and strategic acquisitions and 
collaborations aimed at expanding its operational capabilities, 
enhancing its technological infrastructure, and diversifying its 
product portfolio.
The Board believes that retention of earnings, to fund these 
initiatives is essential to ensure financial flexibility, maintain a 
strong balance sheet, and support sustainable value creation 
for all stakeholders.The Board remains committed to enhancing shareholder 
value and will continue to evaluate the Company’s financial 
performance and capital requirements to determine the 
payment of appropriate dividends in future year.
In accordance with Regulation 43A of SEBI LODR Regulations, 
the Board of Directors of the Company has approved and 
adopted the Dividend Distribution Policy. The Dividend, if any 
shall be payable in accordance with the Dividend Distribution 
Policy, which is available on the website of your Company at  
https:/ /www.ir.ambergroupindia.com/wp-content/
uploads/2025/06/Dividend-Distribution-Policy.pdf ,  
under the “Investor Relations” section.
There has been no change in the said policy during the Financial 
Year 2025 -26.

 PICL is a wholly owned subsidiary of your Company. It

 PICL is engaged in the business of manufacturing

manufacturers of air conditioners, washing machines and 
ceiling fans. The Company also undertakes manufacturing

fans, exhaust fans, three phase motors and general 
purpose motors.
 During the Financial Year 2025-26, PICL has reported 
total revenue of ` 40,294.73 Lakh and a Net Profit of  
` 177.79 Lakh.

CORPORATE GOVERNANCE REQUIREMENTS WITH  
RESPECT TO THE SUBSIDIARIES AND MATERIAL 
SUBSIDIARIES
The Board of Directors of your Company (“the Board”) has 
approved and adopted a Policy for determination of Material 
Subsidiary and Governance of Subsidiary in accordance with 
the provisions of Regulation 16(1)(c) of SEBI LODR Regulations. 
The said policy has been uploaded on the website of the 
Company and it can be viewed at the Web-link: https:/ /www.
ir.ambergroupindia.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/
Policy-for-determination-of-Material-Subsidiary-and-
Governance-of-Subsidiary.pdf .
Further, during the Financial Year 2025-26, Ascent, a 
step-down subsidiary of the Company, was classified as a 
Material Subsidiary under Regulation 16(1)(c) of the SEBI LODR 
Regulations based on the audited financial statements of the 
Company and Ascent for Financial Year 2024–25.
However, subsequent to the closure of Financial Year 2025–26 
and upon review of the latest audited financial statements, 
it has been observed that Ascent no longer meets the 
criteria specified under Regulation 16(1)(c) of the SEBI LODR 
Regulations. Accordingly, Ascent ceased to be a Material 
Subsidiary.
Further, Sidwal also does not qualify as a Material Subsidiary 
under the provisions of Regulation 16 and Regulation 24 of the 
SEBI LODR Regulations, based on the latest audited financial 
statements.
Notwithstanding the above, both Sidwal and Ascent were 
classified as material subsidiaries during Financial Year 
2025–26 and, accordingly, the Company has complied with all 
applicable provisions and governance requirements prescribed 
for material subsidiaries under the SEBI LODR Regulations 
during such period.Director’s Report (Contd.)
Accordingly, as on 31st March 2026, only IL JIN was determined 
as the unlisted material subsidiary of the Company in accordance 
with the SEBI LODR Regulations.
In terms of Regulation 24(1) of the SEBI LODR Regulations, one 
of the Independent Directors of your Company is appointed 
as a Director on the Board of such aforesaid unlisted material 
subsidiary.
The Independent Audit Report of the material subsidiary is 
available on the website of your Company.
The Secretarial Audit Report of such material subsidiaries does 
not contain any qualification, reservation or adverse remark or 
disclaimer.
The Company monitors the performance of subsidiary 
companies, inter alia, by the following means:
•	 Financial statements, in particular investments made by 
unlisted subsidiary companies, are reviewed quarterly by 
your Company’s Audit Committee;
•	 Minutes of Board meetings of the Company’s unlisted 
subsidiary entities are regularly placed before the Board 
of Directors of the Company;
•	 A statement containing all significant transactions 
and arrangements entered into by unlisted subsidiary 
companies is placed before the Company’s Board.
Furthermore, pursuant to Regulation 24(A) of SEBI LODR 
Regulations, as amended, read with the Guidance Note on 
Annual Secretarial Compliance Report issued by the Institute 
of Company Secretaries of India and various circulars issued by 
SEBI, the Secretarial Audit Report (MR-3) of material unlisted 
subsidiaries forms part of this Annual Report.
The other requirements of Regulation 24 of the SEBI LODR 
Regulations with regard to Corporate Governance requirements 
for subsidiary/step-down subsidiary companies have been duly 
complied with.

Board of Directors
The Board of Directors is responsible for and committed to 
sound principles of Corporate Governance in your Company. 
The Board’s focus is on the formulation of business strategies, 
policies and robust control systems. The Board provides 
strategic guidance and direction to your Company in achieving 
its business objectives and protecting the interests of the 
stakeholders.
Matters reserved for the Board are those affecting your 
Company’s overall strategic policies, finances and shareholders. 
These include, but are not restricted to, deliberation of 
business plans, risk management, internal control, preliminary 
announcements of interim and final financial results, dividend 
policy, annual budgets, and major corporate activities such as 
material acquisitions and disposals and connected transactions.
As on the date of this Report, your Company has a professional 
Board with a holistic mix of knowledge, skills and expertise, 
comprising 6 Directors 3 of whom are Independent Directors 
(including a Woman Independent Director) and 3 are Executive 
Directors [in the categories of Executive Chairman & Chief 
Executive Officer, Managing Director and Whole Time Director].

the Board structure.

ANNUAL EVALUATION OF THE BOARD, ITS COMMITTEES 
AND INDIVIDUAL DIRECTORS
The Company has in place a structured framework for the 
evaluation of the performance of the Board, its Committees 
and individual Directors. Pursuant to the provisions of Section 
134(3)(p) of the Act read with Rule 8(4) of the Companies 
(Accounts) Rules, 2014 and Regulations 17(10) and 25(4) of 
the SEBI LODR Regulations, an annual performance evaluation 
of the Board, its Committees, the Chairperson and individual 
Directors was carried out for the Financial Year 2025–26.
The Nomination and Remuneration Committee (“NRC”) 
has formulated the criteria for evaluation of Directors, Key 
Managerial Personnel and Senior Management Personnel in 
accordance with Section 178(2) of the Act read with Regulation 
19(4) and Schedule II Part D of the SEBI LODR Regulations. The 
evaluation criteria include parameters such as attendance and 
participation at meetings, contribution to strategic discussions, 
exercise of independent judgment, domain expertise, 
understanding of the Company’s business and risk framework, 
and effectiveness of Board oversight.
Considering that the NRC is not directly involved in the day-
to-day functioning or performance oversight of other Board-
level Committees, the evaluation of such Committees was 
undertaken by the respective Committees through self-
evaluation. The outcome of these self-evaluations was 
thereafter placed before the Board for its review and noting.
In this regard, self-evaluation forms were circulated to the 
members of the respective Committees along with the agenda papers for their meetings. The Chairpersons of the respective 
Committees submitted summary reports on the performance 
evaluation of their respective Committees to the Board in 
advance.
The evaluation of the performance of the Chairperson was 
carried out by the Independent Directors at their separate 
meeting held on 12th December 2025, taking into account the 
views of the Executive and Non-Executive Directors, as set out 
in the section on “Separate Meeting of Independent Directors” 
herein.
Based on the inputs and summary reports received from the 
respective Committees and individual Directors, the Chairman 
of the Board, Mr. Jasbir Singh, compiled the consolidated 
evaluation reports and presented the same before the Board for 
its consideration. The Board of Directors noted the outcomes 
and expressed its satisfaction with the overall evaluation 
process.
The performance evaluation of Independent and Non-
Independent Directors was undertaken by the Board, excluding 
the Director being evaluated. The evaluation of Board 
Committees was conducted through self-evaluation by the 
respective Committees, the outcomes of which were thereafter 
placed before and noted by the Board.
DIRECTOR’S APPOINTMENT AND REMUNERATION POLICY
Pursuant to Section 134(3)(e), 178(3) and 178(4) of the Act, the 
applicable Rules, and Regulation 19 read with Part D of Schedule 
II of the SEBI LODR Regulations, the NRC of the Board has 
formulated a comprehensive Nomination and Remuneration 
Policy. This policy governs the appointment and determination 
of remuneration for the Directors, KMPs, Senior Management, 
and other employees of the Company.
The salient features of the Policy are as follows:
•	 The NRC has laid down clear criteria for assessing the 
qualifications, positive attributes, and independence of 
Directors, in line with Section 178(3) of the Act.
•	 The Policy provides the framework for determining the 
structure and quantum of remuneration for Executive 
and Non-Executive Directors, including the fixed, variable, 
and commission components, ensuring alignment with 
Company performance and shareholder interests.
•	 Remuneration for Non-Executive and Independent 
Directors is limited to sitting fees and commission within 
statutory limits, as approved by the shareholders on the 
recommendation of NRC and Board.
•	 The compensation structure for Directors, KMPs, Senior 
Management, and other employees is performance 
driven, equitable, and benchmarked against industry best 
practices.Director’s Report (Contd.)

FINANCIAL LIQUIDITY
On standalone basis, cash and cash equivalent as at 31st March 
2026 was ` 7,663.27 Lakh (previous year ` 16,969.76 Lakh). 
The Company has a robust working capital management 
system supported by a well-structured process that enables 
continuous monitoring and control over key parameters such as 
receivables, inventories, and other current assets and liabilities. 
Given the nature of its business, the Company ensures financial 
flexibility by maintaining access to committed credit facilities.
Liquidity is actively managed through rolling forecasts of cash 
flows and regular monitoring of cash and cash equivalents, 
taking into account expected inflows and outflows. The 
Company also considers prevailing market liquidity conditions 
in its operational planning.
As part of its liquidity management policy, the Company 
projects cash flows across major currencies, assesses the 
required level of liquid assets to meet obligations, monitors 
balance sheet liquidity ratios in line with internal benchmarks 
and regulatory requirements, and maintains appropriate debt 
financing arrangements.
Note: Cash and cash equivalents mentioned above includes 
bank deposits with original maturity of less than 3 months.

During the Financial Year 2025–26, based on the 
recommendation of the Audit Committee, the Board approved 
amendments to the Related Party Transactions (RPT) Policy 
at its meeting held on 9th February 2026, to incorporate the 
requisite amendments relating to Related Party Transactions 
under the applicable provisions of the SEBI LODR Regulations.
All related party transactions and subsequent modifications are 
placed before the Audit Committee for its review and approval prior to being entered into. For transactions that are anticipated 
and repetitive in nature, prior approval was duly obtained from 
the Audit Committee in accordance with Regulation 23(2) of the 
SEBI LODR Regulations.
Significant related party transactions undertaken by the 
subsidiaries, where the listed entity is not a party, are also 
placed before the Audit Committee of the Company. For this 
purpose, a transaction is treated as “significant” where its value   
individually or cumulatively during the Financial Year exceeds 
10% of the subsidiary’s annual standalone turnover as per its 
last audited financial statements, in terms of Regulation 23 of 
the SEBI LODR Regulations.
All related party transactions of the Company and its 
subsidiaries are disclosed to the Audit Committee and the 
Board on a quarterly basis in accordance with Regulation 23(3) 
of the SEBI LODR Regulations.
For further details, please refer to the Notes to the Financial 
Statements forming part of this Annual Report.

INTERNAL FINANCIAL CONTROLS AND THEIR ADEQUACY
Your Company has established a comprehensive internal control 
system tailored to the size, nature, scale, and complexity of its 
operations. This system is designed to ensure the safeguarding 
of assets, accurate financial reporting, and compliance with 
applicable laws and regulations.
Key Features of the Internal Control System :
•	 Independent Internal Audit Function:  The Company has 
an independent internal audit team that operates in line 
with best in class governance practices. This team reviews 
and reports to the Audit Committee about compliance 
with internal controls, the efficiency and effectiveness of 
operations, and key process risks.
•	 Audit Committee Oversight:  The Audit Committee 
periodically reviews internal audit plans, significant audit 
findings, and the adequacy of internal controls. This 
ensures that issues, if any are promptly addressed and the 
internal control system remains effective.
•	 Control Self-Assurance:  Systematic self certification of 
adherence to key internal controls by process owners and 
monitors helps in maintaining accountability and ensuring 
that controls are operating as intended.
•	 Information Security Measures:  The Company adheres 
to a comprehensive information security policy and 
continuously upgrades its IT systems to strengthen 
automated controls, thereby mitigating risks associated 
with data breaches and cyber threats.
•	 Management’s Control Testing Initiative:  The internal 
controls were tested as part of the Management’s control 
testing initiative, providing assurance regarding the 
reliability of financial and other records.
The statutory auditors, S.R. Batliboi & Co. LLP, have issued an 
unqualified opinion on the Company’s internal financial controls. 
They have stated that, in their opinion, the Company has, in all 
material respects, adequate internal financial controls with 
reference to the standalone financial statements, and such 
internal financial controls were operating effectively as of 31st 
March 2026.
The Internal Auditors of your Company have direct access to 
the Audit Committee of the Board. Furthermore, the Internal 
Auditors are also responsible for following corrective actions to 
ensure that satisfactory controls are maintained.Director’s Report (Contd.)

Information Technology & Cybersecurity
In today’s digital landscape, addressing IT related concerns such 
as cyber threats and data vulnerabilities is critical to maintaining 
operational integrity and stakeholder trust. Your Company has 
implemented a robust IT infrastructure fortified with advanced 
security protocols and firewalls to mitigate potential risks and 
ensure data protection.
To safeguard user privacy and maintain data security, the 
Company has adopted the following measures:
•	 Network Firewalls : Deployed across the organisation to 
prevent unauthorised access and monitor incoming and 
outgoing traffic.
•	 Antivirus Protection : Installed on all systems to defend 
against viruses, malware, adware, worms, and Trojans.
•	 Strong Password Policy : Enforced across all user 
accounts to prevent unauthorised access and enhance 
account security.
•	 Automated Backups : Scheduled regularly for critical users 
to ensure data recovery and business continuity.
•	 User Awareness & Education : Periodic dissemination 
of the Company’s Security Policy and email awareness campaigns to educate users on best practices and 
potential threats.
•	 Restricted Use of External Drives : External storage 
devices are blocked to prevent data leakage and 
unauthorised data transfers.
These initiatives reflect the Company’s commitment to 
maintaining a secure digital environment and protecting 
sensitive information from evolving cyber threats.

WORKPLACE (PREVENTION, PROHIBITION & REDRESSAL) 
ACT, 2013
Your Company is committed to providing a safe, secure, and 
inclusive workplace environment and has in place a Policy 
on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (“POSH Policy”) in line 
with the provisions of the Sexual Harassment of Women at 
Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 
(“POSH Act”). The Company maintains a zero tolerance policy 
towards sexual harassment.
During the Financial Year 2025-26, your directors noted 
key regulatory developments, including the relaunch of the 
Sexual Harassment Electronic Box (“SHe-Box”), enhanced 
compliance requirements, organisations employing 10 (Ten)
or more employees are required to designate a Nodal Officer 
for coordination and compliance through the SHe-Box portal. 
Accordingly, your Company has designated a Nodal Officer to 
act as a single point of contact for ensuring compliance with 
SHe-Box requirements, including registration, monitoring, and 
reporting.
In light of evolving regulatory expectations and to further 
strengthen governance practices, the Board of Directors of the 
Company approved the adoption of a revised and centralised 
POSH Policy on 9th February 2026, applicable across the Amber 
Group, aimed at ensuring uniform standards, streamlined 
processes, and enhanced oversight.
Further, the Internal Committee (“IC”) was reconstituted in 
accordance with the provisions of the POSH Act. A Group-
level framework has been implemented, with designated 
representatives at various locations to facilitate effective 
implementation and monitoring of POSH compliance.
Key Features of the POSH Policy:
•	 Zero Tolerance & Compliance:  The Policy ensures a zero 
tolerance approach to sexual harassment and is aligned 
with the POSH Act, 2013.
•	 Comprehensive Coverage:  Applicable to all employees 
across the Company, subsidiaries, and joint ventures, 
covering workplace, offsite locations, and virtual 
environments.
•	 Robust Governance Mechanism:  Establishment of 
Internal Committees (ICs) with defined composition and 
a centralised framework across locations for effective 
redressal of complaints related to sexual harassment.
•	 Structured Complaint Redressal:  Defined procedures and 
timelines for complaint handling, including conciliation, 
inquiry, interim relief, and disciplinary actions.
•	 SHe-Box Integration & Safeguards:  Provision for SHe-
Box reporting, appointment of Nodal Officers, along with 
strict confidentiality and non-retaliation measures.Director’s Report (Contd.)

INSIDER TRADING CODE
In adherence to the Securities and Exchange Board of India 
(Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI PIT 
Regulations”), your Company has updated its Code of Conduct 
for regulating, monitoring, and reporting trading activities by 
Designated Persons. These revisions align with the recent 
amendments introduced by SEBI to enhance transparency and 
prevent insider trading.
Key Components of the Updated Code:
•	 Guidelines for Designated Persons:  The Code provides 
clear procedures for Designated Persons regarding the 
handling of Unpublished Price Sensitive Information 
(“UPSI”), pre-clearance of trades, and the reporting of 
transactions. 
•	 Prohibition of Insider Trading:  It strictly prohibits 
Designated Persons from trading in the Company’s 
securities based on UPSI, in line with the SEBI PIT 
Regulations.
•	 Fair Disclosure Practices:  The Company has established 
a Code of Fair Disclosure to ensure timely and transparent 
dissemination of UPSI, safeguarding the interests of all 
stakeholders.
•	 Legitimate Purpose Determination:  A policy for 
determining legitimate purposes for sharing UPSI has 
been implemented, ensuring that such information is 
disclosed only when necessary and appropriate.
•	 Internal Controls and Procedures:  Robust internal 
controls and standardised processes have been instituted 
to ensure compliance with the SEBI PIT Regulations and to 
prevent insider trading activities.
•	 Structured Digital Database:  The Company maintains a 
“Structured Digital Database” containing relevant details 
of Designated Persons and Connected Persons. This 
database monitors the flow of information and internal 
and external communications concerning UPSI, ensuring 
compliance and preventing misuse. 
These measures reflect Company’s commitment to upholding 
the highest standards of corporate governance and ethical 
conduct, fostering a transparent and compliant trading 
environment.The Board of Directors have adopted a Code of Conduct for 
Insider Trading and fair disclosure of Unpublished Price Sensitive 
Information, in accordance with the SEBI PIT Regulations. The 
same can be accessed at the website of the Company i.e. https:/ /
www.ir.ambergroupindia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/
Code-of-conduct-for-insider-trading-and-fair-disclosure-of-
unpublised-price-sensitive-information_17052025.pdf .
During the Financial Year 2025 -26, the Board approved 
amendment to the Code of Conduct for Insider Trading and Fair 
Disclosure of Unpublished Price Sensitive Information at its 
meeting held on 17th May 2025. These changes were made to 
incorporate the amendments to the SEBI PIT Regulations.

7. A description of the method and 
significant assumptions used during 
the year to estimate the fair value 
of options including the following 
informationFair Value Method (Black Scholes Model).
Some of the basic assumptions used in the Black Scholes model are :
Markets are efficient: This assumption suggests that people cannot consistently 
predict the direction of the market or an individual stock. The Black Scholes model 
assumes stocks move in a manner referred to as a random walk. Random walk 
means that at any given moment in time, the price of the underlying stock can go up 
or down with the same probability. The price of the stock in time t+1 is independent 
from the price in time Interest rates remain constant and known. The Black Scholes 
model uses the risk free rate to represent this constant and known rate.
Returns are normally distributed: This assumption suggests returns on the 
underlying stock are normally distributed.
Constant volatility: The most significant assumption is that volatility, a measure 
of how much a stock can be expected to move in the near term, is a constant 
over time. While volatility can be relatively constant in very short term, it is never 
constant in longer term. Some advanced option valuation models substitute Black 
Scholes constant volatility with stochastic process generated estimates.
Liquidity: The Black Scholes model assumes that markets are perfectly liquid and it 
is possible to purchase or sell any amount of stock or options or their fractions at 
any given time.(a) the weighted-average values

(i) Scheme of Amalgamation of Ever Electronics Private

(ii) Formation of Joint Venture
 A Joint Venture Agreement was entered into between

pioneer in the field of printed circuit boards (“PCBs”), on  
15th October 2024, for the incorporation of a Joint Venture 
Company in India (“JVC”) to undertake the business of 
manufacturing, assembling and selling HDI, Flex, and 
Semiconductor Substrate PCBs (“Business”).
 Pursuant to the said Joint Venture Agreement, the JVC, 
namely Ascent–K Circuit Private Limited, was incorporated 
on 7th April 2025.
 The Company has subscribed to 7,00,000 equity shares 
aggregating to `70,00,000, whereas Korea Circuit 
Co. Limited has subscribed to 3,00,000 equity shares 
aggregating to `30,00,000.
 Consequent to the composition of the Board of Directors 
and control over decision- making, Ascent–K Circuit Private 
Limited is treated as a subsidiary of the Company.

step-down Wholly Owned Subsidiary of Amber. 
 ILJIN Holding Ltd acted as a dedicated investment vehicle

in multiple tranches. Pursuant to the definitive agreements, the Company, 
through its Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) and wholly 
owned subsidiary, ILJIN Holding, acquired a 40.20% stake 
in Unitronics on 9th October 2025 and subsequently 
Unitronics became the subsidiary of ILJIN Holding and a 
step-down subsidiary of the Company and Amber.
 Subsequently, the Company undertook additional 
acquisitions from time to time, resulting in ILJIN Holding 
increasing its ownership stake to 49.66% of the equity 
share capital of Unitronics as of 31st March 2026.
 As a result of these acquisitions, Unitronics has become 
a subsidiary of ILJIN Holding and, consequently, a step-
down subsidiary of the Company and Amber.

1. Brief outline of the Company’s CSR policy, including 
overview of projects or programmes proposed to be 
undertaken :
 Over the years, your Company is making impressive strides 
towards sustainability and social responsibility. As a good 
corporate citizen, your Company upholds a value system 
that mandates sustainability at every level of our value 
chain and in every aspect of our business. We understand 
that our Corporate Social Responsibility (“CSR”) initiatives 
are crucial for safeguarding the environment, promoting 
socio-economic progress, and preserving the natural 
world.
 Your Company engages in numerous activities aimed 
at preserving and enhancing environmental resources 
impacted by human activity. Our strong community 
relations help us build goodwill and trust among our 
stakeholders, enabling us to continue our growth journey 
and contribute to the well being of the community. Our CSR 
initiatives exhibit our commitment to creating empowered 
citizens and enhancing the lives of those in need, leading 
to a safer and more sustainable future.
 The Board of Directors of your Company has adopted 
the CSR policy with several key points. These include 
directing our CSR programmes towards goals such as 
enhancing environmental and natural capital, supporting 
rural development, woman empowerment, promoting 
education including skill development, providing preventive 
healthcare, sanitation, and drinking water, creating 
livelihoods for disadvantaged sections of society in rural 
and urban India, and preserving & promoting sports. We 
are also focused on developing the necessary capability 
and self reliance of beneficiaries at the grassroots level, 
as these are prerequisites for social and economic ANNUAL REPORT ON CSR PROJECTS/ACTIVITIES  
(Pursuant to Section 135 of the Act)
development.
 Our affirmative actions include skill building and 
vocational training to enhance employability and 
generate livelihoods for disadvantaged sections of 
society. We pursue CSR programmes primarily in areas 
near our operations to ensure close supervision and 
maximum development impact. Additionally, we engage 
in activities during natural calamities or participate in 
Disaster Management Systems, contribute to rural 
sports, nationally recognised sports, Paralympic sports 
& Olympic sports, and support various relief funds set up 
by the Central Government.
 Your Company is committed to making substantial 
improvements in the social framework of nearby 
communities. During the Financial Year 2025 -26, our 
initiatives to promote education and healthcare were 
the primary focus of attention. Our key CSR focus areas 
include health and education, women empowerment, 
vocational skill development, promoting gender equality, 
and developmental projects in rural areas such as safe 
drinking water facilities and access to basic sanitation.
 Some of our key CSR initiatives undertaken during the 
Financial Year 2025-26 include empowering societies by

4 Climate Action Climate change presents a 
multi-dimensional risk to our 
manufacturing operations 
in Financial Year 2025-26. 
Our facilities involve energy 
intensive manufacturing 
processes that are significant 
consumers of electricity and 
thermal energy, contributing 
to Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG 
emissions. Physical climate 
risks including extreme 
weather events, flooding, 
and water stress can disrupt 
operations, affect raw material 
availability, and impact 
logistics networks.
Transition risks are equally 
material: Tightening energy 
efficiency norms under the 
Bureau of Energy Efficiency 
(BEE), India's updated 
Nationally Determined 
Contributions (NDCs), SEBI's 
BRSR Core assured disclosure 
requirements, and evolving 
environmental regulations 
all create regulatory and 
commercial adaptation 
imperatives for our business.
Our OEM and ODM customers 
including large listed consumer 
durable and automotive brands 
with public sustainability 
commitments are increasingly 
embedding Scope 3 emissions 
tracking and supplier carbon 
performance criteria in their 
procurement frameworks. 
Failure to demonstrate 
credible climate action could 
risk our approved vendor 
status with environmentally 
progressive customers.Our Climate Action Strategy 
for the Financial Year 2025-26 
encompasses:
•    GHG Emissions Inventory and 
Reduction Targets: Systematic 
tracking of Scope 1 and 
Scope 2 emissions across all 
manufacturing facilities, with 
defined reduction targets aligned 
with BRSR Core disclosure 
requirements.
•    Renewable Energy Transition: 
Expansion of on-site solar power 
capacity and evaluation of Power 
Purchase Agreements (PPAs) 
for green electricity, targeting 
reduced dependence on grid 
power for energy intensive 
manufacturing processes.
•    Energy Efficiency in 
Manufacturing: Implementation 
of energy management 
systems, variable frequency 
drives, waste heat recovery, 
and LED lighting retrofits across 
all facilities to reduce specific 
energy consumption.
•    Climate Risk Assessment: 
Integration of physical 
and transition climate risk 
assessments into business 
continuity and strategic planning 
frameworks, with particular 
focus on supply chain resilience 
for key raw materials.
•    Regulatory Transition Readiness: 
Proactive investment in R&D and 
capability adaptation to ensure 
our manufacturing processes 
remain aligned with evolving 
environmental regulations.
•    Supplier Engagement: Engaging 
key raw material suppliers on 
emissions reporting and energy 
efficiency to support our evolving 
Scope 3 disclosure obligations 
under BRSR Core.Negative (if unmitigated):
•    Increased energy costs from 
carbon pricing mechanisms 
or energy surcharges could 
materially impact operating 
costs across energy intensive 
manufacturing processes.
•    Physical disruptions to raw 
material supply chains from 
climate events could cause 
production stoppages and 
force unplanned procurement 
at elevated spot prices.
•    Loss of OEM/ODM customer

met.
•    Regulatory non-compliance

Positive (if well managed):

directly improving EBITDA 
margins.
•    Proactive climate

our ESG profile with

5 Occupational 
Health and 
SafetyOur manufacturing operations 
span a range of processes that 
involve inherent occupational 
hazards, including exposure 
to heat, noise, chemical 
agents, moving machinery, 
and ergonomic risk factors. 
Rigorous and sustained OHS 
management is therefore 
essential to protect the well 
being of our workforce and 
ensure operational continuity.
The Occupational Safety, 
Health and Working 
Conditions Code, 2020 and 
its implementing rules have 
significantly strengthened 
OHS compliance obligations 
for manufacturing 
establishments. Our 
operations also involve 
substantial contractor and 
contract labour workforce 
engagement, whose safety 
management requires 
dedicated and structured 
oversight.
OHS performance is 
increasingly scrutinised by our 
OEM and ODM customers as 
part of supplier sustainability 
audits. Any significant 
workplace incident can disrupt 
production commitments, 
impact customer confidence, 
and affect our standing as an 
employer of choice.Our OHS management framework 
for Financial Year  2025 - 26 
includes:
•    Hazard Identification and Risk 
Assessment (HIRA): Systematic 
identification and risk-ranking 
of workplace hazards across all 
manufacturing operations, with 
controls implemented per the 
hierarchy of controls principle.
•    Behaviour Based Safety (BBS) 
Programme: Structured BBS 
observations and near miss 
reporting culture to proactively 
identify and address at risk 
behaviours before they result in 
incidents.
•    Contractor Safety Management: 
Pre-qualification, induction, 
and ongoing monitoring of all 
contractor and contract labour 
personnel to ensure consistent 
application of OHS standards 
across all workforce categories.
•    Periodic Safety Audits and 
Gemba Walks: Regular 
independent safety audits at 
all manufacturing facilities, 
complemented by Plant Head 
led Gemba walks to maintain 
visible leadership commitment 
to shop floor safety.
•    Emergency Preparedness: 
Maintained and regularly 
tested emergency response 
plans relevant to our specific 
manufacturing risk profile.
•    Incident Investigation and Cross 
Plant Learning: Root cause 
analysis of all incidents and 
near misses, with structured 
dissemination of learnings 
and corrective actions across 
all group plants to prevent 
recurrence.Positive (from effective OHS 
management):
•    Reduction in Lost Time 
Injury Frequency Rate 
(LTIFR) avoids direct costs 
from worker compensation, 
medical expenses, regulatory 
penalties, and production 
downtime particularly 
critical in high volume OEM 
supply environments where 
delivery schedules are tightly 
managed.
•    Strong OHS performance 
supports favourable 
outcomes in customer 
supplier audits, protecting 
approved vendor status with 
OEM customers who embed 
HSE standards in supply 
chain assessments.
•    A safe and well managed 
workplace enhances 
employee engagement, 
reduces absenteeism, and 
improves retention of skilled 
manufacturing personnel.
Negative (if OHS risks are 
inadequately managed):
•    Serious workplace accidents 
can result in worker 
compensation liability, 
regulatory enforcement 
action, and potential criminal 
prosecution of responsible 
officers.
•    Production disruptions arising 
from OHS incidents can cause 
customer delivery failures 
and contractual penalties, 
particularly in just in time 
OEM supply arrangements.

•    Dedicated HR Teams: Each

9 Supply Chain 
ManagementOur manufacturing operations 
are dependent on a complex 
multi-tier supply chain 
spanning metallic raw 
materials, engineering 
polymers, and other industrial 
inputs sourced from domestic 
and international suppliers. 
Supply chain disruptions 
whether from geopolitical 
events, commodity market 
volatility, logistics constraints, 
or supplier financial distress 
can directly impact our 
production schedules and our 
ability to fulfil OEM customer 
delivery commitments.
Key raw materials are globally 
traded commodities subject 
to significant price volatility. 
Import dependency for certain 
specialty inputs adds foreign 
exchange and logistics risk. 
Concentration risk from sole 
source or limited source 
supply arrangements for 
critical inputs amplifies 
vulnerability to disruption.
Our OEM customers 
operate on tight production 
schedules and just in time 
inventory models, meaning 
supply chain failures on our 
part translate rapidly into 
customer line stoppages 
and contractual penalties. 
Evolving ESG traceability 
requirements from OEM 
customers also necessitate 
greater transparency and 
documentation across our 
supply base.Our supply chain risk mitigation 
strategy encompasses:
•    Supplier Diversification: 
Maintaining qualified alternate 
suppliers for critical raw 
materials to eliminate single 
source dependencies and ensure 
supply continuity across all 
manufacturing operations.
•    Commodity Price Risk 
Management: Monitoring of key 
commodity prices and evaluation 
of forward procurement and 
hedging strategies to manage 
input cost volatility.
•    Supplier Financial and 
Compliance Assessment: 
Periodic evaluation of key 
suppliers on financial stability, 
regulatory compliance, quality 
systems, and sustainability 
practices, with early warning 
mechanisms for at risk suppliers.
•    Digital Procurement Platform: 
Utilisation of e-auction tools, 
vendor portals, and supplier 
performance dashboards 
to ensure procurement 
transparency, data accuracy, and 
competitive sourcing.
•    Strategic Safety Stock: 
Maintenance of appropriate 
inventory buffers for long lead 
and high criticality inputs to 
protect against short term 
supply disruptions.
•    Vendor Code of Conduct: 
Enforcement of supply chain 
ethical and environmental 
standards through our Supplier 
Code of Conduct, covering 
labour rights, environmental 
compliance, and anti corruption.Negative (if risks are not 
managed):
•    Supply disruptions causing 
production stoppages result 
in loss of revenue, overtime 
and expediting costs, 
and potential contractual 
penalties from OEM 
customers operating just in 
time supply arrangements.
•    Raw material price spikes 
can significantly compress 
gross margins if not 
adequately managed through 
procurement strategy or 
contractual pass-through 
mechanisms with customers.
•    Compliance failures by supply 
chain partners can result 
in disqualification by ESG 
conscious OEM customers 
and reputational damage to 
the Company.
